builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Density Feedback Control for Transferability of Generative Sparse Adversarial Attacks
summary: DFC replaces the fixed sparsity coefficient in generator-based sparse adversarial attack training with a per-epoch feedback controller that adjusts the coefficient based on the gap between observed hard-mask density and a target density, without changing the generator architecture or loss. The cost is minimal: a density computation and coefficient update once per epoch, with no extra memory or inference overhead. It can fail to help when the attack constrains perturbations to source-model feature-importance regions, as the paper reports no consistent gain for EGS-TSSA, and gains may not hold at densities far from the tested 10% target.
rationale: DFC is a low-cost training-controller addition that removes manual re-tuning of the sparsity coefficient and is feasible on a single 24 GB GPU, but it matters only if the reader performs adversarial robustness evaluation and its benefit is attack-dependent, as shown by the null result on EGS-TSSA.
technique: Density feedback control for sparse adversarial attacks

claims.statement: DFC replaces the fixed sparsity coefficient in generator-based sparse adversarial attack training with a per-epoch feedback controller that adjusts the coefficient based on the gap between observed hard-mask density and a target density, without changing the generator architecture or loss. The cost is minimal: a density computation and coefficient update once per epoch, with no extra memory or inference overhead. It can fail to help when the attack constrains perturbations to source-model feature-importance regions, as the paper reports no consistent gain for EGS-TSSA, and gains may not hold at densities far from the tested 10% target.

At a 10% target density, DFC brings the mean density of three generator-based sparse attacks within one percentage point of target in a single run and improves transfer attack success rate for two of them on CNN and Transformer targets while perturbing fewer pixels; no multiplicative improvement factor is reported.
